newsitem.title: UK: Thailand on course for record cane crop - Czarnikow.
newsitem.headline: Thailand on course for record cane crop - Czarnikow.

text.p: Thailand is still on course to produce a record sugar cane crop in 1996/97 despite a delayed start to harvesting operations, Czarnikow Sugar said in a report on Thursday.
It said a number of factors had contributed to the delay but sugar extraction rates were rising and cane output was still estimated at 60 million tonnes.
Growers were opting to leave the crop in the ground in the hope of higher production, while the rice harvest had been problematic and caused reduced availability of field workers to cut cane.
"Nevertheless, it is still likely that a new record crop could be produced in 1996/97," it said.
While the key variable would be the total amount of cane which would eventually be harvested, the pre-season rains were likely to have increased the cane potential, Czarnikow said.
Sugar extraction rates had also improved, it added.
"Despite the low early levels it may still be possible for the final rate to reach 10.5 percent," the report said.
It added that the low early yields were caused by a delayed start rather than poor cane or operational problems.
